title: Follow-ups from pr-reviewer's review of PR #181 (frontend-trade-journal-followups)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #181 (frontend-trade-journal-followups), recorded here so they aren't lost once the PR merges and the review comment scrolls out of view.

checklist.step: TradeJournalPanel.test.tsx's new 'sorts by a nullable grade column, missing values last' test doesn't actually exercise a null value in the column it sorts: both fixture rows have a non-null buy_grade_pct (40 and 90) -- only sell_grade_pct/trade_grade_pct (columns not being sorted in that test) are null. So the test only verifies ordinary ascending numeric sort, not the null-last claim its own name/comment makes for this call site (unlike PositionsTable.test.tsx's equivalent current_price sort test, which does use a real null in the sorted column). Manually verified in a live browser walkthrough that TradeJournalPanel's null-last sorting is in fact correct (a closed trade with all-null grades sorted to the last row in both ascending and descending order on Buy Grade) -- so this is a test-honesty/coverage gap, not a functional bug. Worth adding a genuine null case to that test (e.g. give one row a null buy_grade_pct) so the assertion matches what it claims to check.

decisions.decision: Added a third fixture row (ticker CCC) with buy_grade_pct: null to TradeJournalPanel.test.tsx's 'sorts by a nullable grade column, missing values last' test, and extended the assertion to check both ascending (AAA, BBB, CCC -- null last) and descending (BBB, AAA, CCC -- null still last, not first) order after clicking the Buy Grade header twice. Implemented as part of a batched PR (#208) alongside four other unrelated small follow-up tasks, per explicit user instruction to batch remaining small followups onto one branch/PR.
decisions.rationale: A genuine null in the sorted column (not just the two other, unsorted grade columns the test already varied) is exactly what the finding asked for -- it's the only way this test can actually fail if a future change broke the null-last sort behavior it claims to verify. Added the descending-order check too (not just ascending) since 'missing values last' is specifically claimed regardless of sort direction, per the finding's own manual-verification note ('sorted to the last row in both ascending and descending order') -- asserting only ascending would have left that half of the claim just as untested as before.

comments.summary: TradeJournalPanel.test.tsx's 'sorts by a nullable grade column, missing values last' test now includes a genuine null buy_grade_pct row (CCC) and asserts null-last ordering in both ascending and descending order after clicking the Buy Grade header, matching what the test's own name claims and mirroring PositionsTable.test.tsx's precedent.

review.notes: Part of a 5-task batched PR (#208). Full frontend suite (700 tests, 99.7%+ coverage), eslint, and tsc -b --noEmit all clean.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran backend suite (935 passed, 99.94% cov, mypy clean) and frontend suite (700 passed, 99.72%+ statement/99.19% branch cov, tsc -b --noEmit clean, eslint clean). Read the diff myself: confirmed TradeJournalPanel.test.tsx's updated 'sorts by a nullable grade column' test adds a genuine null buy_grade_pct row (CCC) and asserts null-last ordering in both ascending and descending order after clicking Buy Grade. Ran scripts/validate_tasks.py (no violations).
